title: Chelsea fined £10m for breaching agent payment rules
dek: The Football Association fined Chelsea £10m and imposed a suspended two-window registration ban for breaching agent payment rules between 2009 and 2022. The violations span 13 years of the club's player acquisition operations.
author: The GoCheckMySports Desk
key_fact: Chelsea received a £10m fine and suspended two-window registration ban from the FA for systemic agent payment rule violations over 13 years (2009-2022).
bottom_line: The fine represents a material penalty for systemic non-compliance but leaves open the mechanics of enforcement for the suspended ban. Watch whether the FA clarifies what future conduct would activate the registration prohibition, and whether other clubs face similar investigations for agent payment practices.
body: The Football Association fined Chelsea £10m and imposed a suspended two-window registration ban for breaching rules relating to payments to agents between 2009 and 2022, per BBC Sport.

The violations span a 13-year period covering a substantial portion of the club's modern acquisition activity. The suspended two-window registration ban means Chelsea would face a two-window transfer prohibition if the FA deems the club in further breach of agent payment regulations, though the conditions triggering that ban were not specified in the FA's announcement.
